facts.name: Cosmos
facts.color: Pink, magenta, crimson or white daisies (pink shown)
facts.light: Full sun; poor to average, well-drained soil
facts.moisture: Dry to average; takes dry spells once growing
facts.notes: Tall, airy plants with feathery leaves and big daisy flowers from midsummer until frost; bees and butterflies love them. An annual: plant after the last frost in late May. Skip the fertilizer (rich soil makes floppy plants), and snip off faded flowers to keep it blooming and to stop it from seeding everywhere.

sources.title: MIgardener (Michigan seed company): Picotee Cosmo
sources.note: Cosmos bipinnatus seed sold by a Michigan company with a store in St. Clair, MI; easy to grow, about 2 ft and up.

sources.title: Utah State University Extension: Cosmos in the Garden
sources.note: Space cosmos 1 to 2 ft apart; closer plants hold each other up. Once growing it needs little water, no fertilizer and little care.

sources.title: Oregon State University Extension: Cheery garden cosmos
sources.note: Garden cosmos (Cosmos bipinnatus) is still blooming strong into September, an easy pollinator annual.

sources.title: Rutgers NJAES: Landscape Plants Rated by Deer Resistance (printable list)
sources.note: Annuals: calendula and strawflower are rated A (rarely damaged); California poppy, verbena and zinnia B (seldom severely damaged); cosmos C (occasionally severely damaged).

sources.title: Cats Protection: Safe plants guide
sources.note: Cosmos is on the list of plants safe for cats. ASPCA doesn't list cosmos either way.

companions.why: Cosmos gives zinnias a contrast in height and texture.

sources.title: Gardenia: Zinnia Flowers, a must-have for every garden
